brief_text: I run operations at our Leeds parcel depot and our on-time delivery rate has slipped to about 86% over the last quarter — head office wants it back to at least 94% by the end of March. I'm weighing three things: adding an evening sort shift so vans leave fully loaded by 7am, buying the route-planning software the vendor keeps pitching (they claim it lifts on-time by 3 to 6 points, which I'd take with a pinch of salt), or moving city-centre drops to two micro-hubs with cargo bikes. I've got roughly £150k to spend this financial year and nothing more. The evening shift would cost around £90k a year in wages, the software about £60k, and the micro-hubs probably £140k to set up. Big worry is the December peak — if anything we change goes wrong mid-peak we could drop well below where we are now. I'd honestly rather not lean on more agency staff if we can avoid it, the quality has been patchy.
